answers.evidence: s56001–04 puts Foster on the east bank of the South Branch on 8 October 1871, having just crossed the bridge with the fire opposite him.
s56006–13 asks whether fire will appear behind him and whether brick streets or another bridge will hold; the opening gives none of those outcomes.
After the permitted opening flashback, the same fire advances from the west bank through Foster's crossings and the North Side witnessed by Losch; events move forward in time.
The opening and chapter bridges pose questions about concrete places and actions; they do not announce an outline or recite an upcoming list.

The next chapters take up the preceding object or question: the earlier river fire at s56014, Foster after the bell at s56042, the east bank at s56070, brick streets at s56093, Losch at s56117, and the water shortage at s56145.
Unanswered questions recur well inside 90 seconds, including the river at s56029, the roof at s56057, the east-bank fire at s56069, stone buildings at s56092, and the North Side bridge at s56115.

The house behind Foster catches at s56073–79, the church roof at s56058–63, stone buildings at s56103–08, the northern bridge at s56136–38, and the threatened grassland is spared by rain at s56166–67.

The repeated east-bank and northern-resident moments are named callbacks at s56073 and s56129, followed by new outcomes; later returns to flying debris occur in new locations rather than retelling the same incident.
Headings name developments such as a new fire behind the water, the stone city hall failing, and rain after the pumping station's loss.
s56172–76 closes on the limits of the river as a safety line, with no mention of another episode or film.

After the riverbank scene, s56007, s56010–11, and s56012 preview distinct later moments: houses behind Foster, the brick quarter and bridge, and a North Side resident's view; each withholds its result.

The concrete problem is where a fleeing resident can stand beyond the advancing fire: Foster tests the river, stone district, and North Side, while Losch carries the same fire's northern advance to its end.

s56153–71 spends about two minutes on Losch's grassland shelter, furrows, fence posts, wet clothes, rain, and sleep after the river-crossing mechanism and northern bridge are resolved at s56073–88 and s56136. Most of this coda does not advance why river water failed to stop the fire.
